goal: Implement v3 lexicon package — Phase 0/1 + distribution (consumer-driven). Foundation: extract Span from ast/ to a top-level shared base (slop/span.py; ast and component.identity re-export, no consumer import changes); add ast.Node.identifiers()->Iterator[(str,Span)], absorbing the inline identifier walk in model/lexicon.build_lexicon. Stand up top-level slop/lexicon/ package: roles.py (Role enum MODULE/PACKAGE/CLASS/CALLABLE/PARAMETER/BODY_REF), stopwords.py (UNIVERSAL_NOISE, injectable), tokenize.py (split_tokens + Lexeme), corpus.py (Lexicon over (text,role,span)). Bridge build_lexicon stays in component/model layer (above both packages): calls Node.identifiers(), tags Role, unions fs-derived names, feeds lexicon.Lexicon; re-point model/components.py. Proof gate: vocabulary rule output byte-identical before/after (golden test). Then port distribution.py (Zipf fit + narrate) and route vocabulary through it. Deferred: collocations/affix/FCA (until their rule), cross-view batteries (blocked on structure design), diagnostic harness. Boundary discipline: no threshold/verdict in lexicon/; kernel uses lexicographic names.

summary.title: v3 lexicon implemented: Span extracted, Node.identifiers(), standalone slop/lexicon/ + distribution
summary.what: Phase 0/1 + distribution of the lexicon package, committed at d1945fc. (1) Extracted Span to top-level slop/span.py (zero-dep shared base; ast + component.identity re-export). (2) Added ast.Node.identifiers() using the grammar's NodeKind.IDENTIFIER classification, replacing the endswith('_identifier') heuristic; byte-identical for Python, fixes scoped_identifier double-count/garbage tokens for C++/Rust/Go/TS. (3) Stood up slop/lexicon/ as a standalone linguistic kernel (roles/stopwords/tokenize/corpus/distribution) importing nothing above span. (4) Bridge build_lexicon tags Role + unions fs names; vocabulary rule routed through Lexicon.distribution() (Zipf + narrate). 69 tests pass; boundary litmus verified (slop.lexicon imports only slop.lexicon.* + slop.span).
summary.why: Give identifier vocabulary one owner, mirroring the ast extraction: a self-contained kernel usable outside the linter, with slop's invented metrics kept above it. Unblocks the scope-layer extraction that follows.

decisions.chose: grammar NodeKind.IDENTIFIER classification, not a name-shape heuristic
decisions.rationale: More correct (no scoped_identifier double-count/garbage), idiomatic (tabular dispatch), byte-identical for Python.

decisions.chose: full enum incl. REALM; emit REALM/PACKAGE/MODULE + BODY_REF now, reserve CLASS/CALLABLE/PARAMETER
decisions.rationale: Establish the interface; no consumer reads finer roles yet and name/param spans aren't plumbed (consumer-driven).

decisions.chose: TokenDistribution + Zipf + narrate; dropped histogram/Summary + ConceptOwnership
decisions.rationale: Consumer-driven: vocabulary is the only consumer; the dropped pieces have none (ConceptOwnership is corpus-blocked).
Claim-free evidence, no verdict/threshold; flagged to user as the one debatable boundary call.

rejected.reason: Double-counts nested identifiers and leaks punctuated pseudo-tokens; violates tabular-dispatch rule.
Would forfeit the standalone-usable kernel; lexicon stays the kernel, slop signals live above.

architectural_claims: slop.lexicon is a standalone linguistic kernel importing only slop.span + stdlib; usable outside the linter.
Span is the shared substrate location primitive at the package root; ast and lexicon are peers depending on it.
ast.Node.identifiers() is the AST's identifier contribution; the lexicon decides what counts as vocabulary.
migration_notes: Multi-language identifier token sets change (correctly) vs the old heuristic; Python unchanged. No non-Python lexicon test yet — add when touching multi-language.
